t: The Oxus civilisation was a Middle Bronze Age culture of walled towns in present-day Turkmenistan, Afghanistan and Uzbekistan, named the BMAC by Viktor Sarianidi in 1976.
Its farmers irrigated wheat and barley, its craftspeople worked bronze, copper, silver and gold, and its towns traded with the Indus Valley, the Iranian Plateau and the Persian Gulf.
Its link with the Indo-Iranians is debated; DNA shows its people descended mainly from local farmers related to those of the Iranian plateau, later mixing with steppe herders.
dyk: A model of a cart drawn by a camel, from about 2200 BCE, was found at Altyn Depe: camels were domesticated within the Oxus civilisation.
ev: Models of two-wheeled carts at Altyn Depe give the earliest evidence of wheeled transport in Central Asia
Altyn Depe in the Kopet Dag foothills develops a proto-urban society
The urban Integration Era begins, by different datings, with walled centres such as Namazga Depe, Altyn Depe, Kelleli and Gonur Depe
A foal is buried on a four-wheeled wagon with bronze-banded wheels in the Royal Necropolis at Gonur Depe
Contacts with the peoples of the Eurasian steppes to the north intensify
The walled centres shrink sharply, and Tazabagyab-Andronovo pottery spreads through the Bactrian and Margian countryside
The urban phase ends, by Dubova and Lyonnet’s dating
Viktor Sarianidi names the complex the Bactria–Margiana Archaeological Complex

f.homeland: Southern Turkmenistan (the Kopet Dag foothills and Margiana in the Murghab delta), northern Afghanistan (southern Bactria), southern Uzbekistan, southwestern Tajikistan and northeastern Iran; key sites Gonur Depe, Togolok, Kelleli, Altyn Depe, Namazga Depe, Dashly 3 and Sappali Tepe.
f.period: It thrived c. 2500–1700 BCE; its urban Integration Era is dated c. 2400–1950 BCE by Sandro Salvatori and c. 2250–1700 BCE by Nadezhda Dubova and Bertille Lyonnet; its walled centres shrank sharply c. 1900 BCE.
f.known: fortified towns and palaces with massive walls and gates; irrigation farming of wheat and barley; bronze, copper, silver and gold metalwork; “Bactrian princess” figurines; early wheeled carts and domesticated camels; a foal buried on a wagon at Gonur Depe
f.sources: Soviet excavations, above all by Viktor Sarianidi from 1969; later Italian, French, Russian and Iranian fieldwork; radiocarbon dating; ancient DNA (Narasimhan and colleagues, 2019); proposed loanwords in the Indo-Iranian languages.
